lesson.title: Checking note titles before saving them in createNote
lesson.summary: The agent added a check to the createNote function in notes.js. Now a note title must be text, must not be blank, and can be at most 100 characters long. If the title breaks a rule, the code stops and shows a clear error message. The agent also added 5 new tests to notes.test.js and ran them with `node --test`. All 6 tests passed. No git commands appear in the steps.

asks.text: Add validation to createNote in notes.js so the title must be a non-empty string
asks.evidence: The diff adds `typeof title !== 'string'` and `title.trim() === ''` checks at the top of createNote.

asks.text: The title must be at most 100 characters
asks.evidence: The diff adds `const MAX_TITLE_LENGTH = 100;` and a check `title.length > MAX_TITLE_LENGTH`.

asks.text: Otherwise throw an Error with a clear message
asks.evidence: Each check runs `throw new Error(...)` with a message such as 'Note title must not be empty'.
notes.test.js got 26 new lines, which make up 5 new tests (edit at 00:16).
The steps show only Glob, Read, Edit and one Bash command (`node --test`). There is no git command.

lesson.why: Before this change, createNote accepted anything as a title: nothing, a number, an empty string, or a very long text. Bad data could get into the notes list. The user wanted a guard at the door so only sensible titles get in.
how: Looked at all files in the project (Glob), then read notes.js, notes.test.js and package.json.
Added a constant MAX_TITLE_LENGTH = 100 at the top of notes.js.
Added three checks at the start of createNote: is it text? Is it blank (spaces count as blank)? Is it longer than 100 characters? Each failed check throws an Error with a clear message.
Added 5 tests: non-text titles, empty and spaces-only titles, a 101-character title, a title of exactly 100 characters, and a test that a failed call does not save a note.
lesson.before: createNote saved a note with any title at all, even `undefined`, `''` or a 500-character text.
lesson.after: createNote first checks the title. It stops with an error like 'Note title must be a string, got number', 'Note title must not be empty' or 'Note title must be at most 100 characters, got 101'. Only valid titles are saved.

notes.text: The three checks run before `nextId++`. So a rejected title does not use up an id number, and nothing is added to the notes Map.
The agent's thinking is not available. In its final reply, it says it chose to treat spaces-only titles like '   ' as empty. It asks you to confirm this choice.
The new tests use `assert.throws` with a pattern for the message, so they check the wording of each error too.

impact.why: '  Shopping  ' passes the check and is saved with its spaces, because only the blank check uses trim. This may or may not be what you want.
impact.fix: Decide whether to save `title.trim()` instead of the raw title.

impact.title: Emoji count as 2 characters
impact.why: JavaScript's `.length` counts some symbols, like many emoji, as 2. A title of 60 emoji could be rejected as 120 characters.
impact.fix: This only matters if titles often contain emoji. If so, count with `[...title].length`.

concepts.name: Validation
concepts.explain: Checking data before you use it, like a bouncer checking tickets at a door.

concepts.name: Function (createNote)
concepts.explain: A named, reusable block of code. createNote takes a title and a body and makes a note.

concepts.name: throw new Error
concepts.explain: A way to stop the code and raise an alarm with a message that explains what went wrong.

concepts.name: String
concepts.explain: A piece of text, like 'Shopping'. Numbers, null and lists are not strings.

concepts.name: trim()
concepts.explain: Removes spaces from the start and end of text. '   '.trim() becomes '', which counts as empty.

concepts.name: typeof
concepts.explain: A JavaScript word that tells you what kind of value something is, such as 'string' or 'number'.

concepts.name: Test
concepts.explain: A small program that runs your code and checks the result is what you expect.

concepts.name: node --test
concepts.explain: The command that tells Node.js to find and run the test files in the project.

concepts.name: assert.throws
concepts.explain: A test helper that passes only if the code inside it raises an error.

lesson.title: Adding a deleteNote(id) function to the notes app
lesson.summary: The agent added a new function called deleteNote to notes.js. You give it a note's id and it removes that note. It gives back true if a note was removed, or false if no note had that id. The agent also wrote 3 new tests in notes.test.js. It ran all the tests with node --test, and all 9 passed. It did not use git.

asks.evidence: The diff adds `export function deleteNote(id) { return notes.delete(id); }` to notes.js (edit at 00:03).
The test 'deletes an existing note and returns true' checks that after deleting, getNote gives null and listNotes no longer has the note. It passed at 00:13.

asks.text: Return true if the note was removed, false if it did not exist
asks.evidence: The tests 'deletes an existing note and returns true', 'returns false when deleting a note that does not exist' and 'returns false when deleting the same note twice' all passed at 00:13.
The steps show only file edits and one `node --test` command. No git command was run.

lesson.why: The notes app could already create, read and list notes, but it had no way to remove one. The user wanted a delete feature that also says whether it worked: true means a note was removed, false means there was nothing to remove.
how: Added a new function `deleteNote(id)` to notes.js, between `getNote` and `listNotes`.

Wrote the function as one line: `return notes.delete(id);`. The note store (`notes`) already has a delete action that removes an item and gives back true or false, so the new function just passes that answer back.
Added `deleteNote` to the import line at the top of notes.test.js so the tests can use it.
Wrote 3 new tests: delete an existing note, delete an id that does not exist, and delete the same note twice.
Ran `node --test`. All 9 tests passed (6 old ones and 3 new ones).
lesson.before: Notes could be created, read and listed, but there was no way to remove a note.
lesson.after: `deleteNote(id)` removes a note. It returns true if the note existed and was removed, and false if no note had that id, including when you try to delete the same note a second time.

notes.text: Added 4 lines: the new exported function `deleteNote(id)`, which calls `notes.delete(id)` and returns its true/false answer.
Changed the import line to include `deleteNote` and added 3 tests about deleting notes (+18 lines, -1 line).

impact.title: A text id like '1' will not match a number id like 1
impact.why: If an id comes in as text, for example from a web address, the delete will quietly return false even though the note exists. The agent pointed this out but did not change the code. getNote behaves the same way.
impact.fix: Turn the id into a number before calling deleteNote, or make deleteNote do that itself.

impact.title: Tests share one note store
impact.why: All tests use the same notes in memory, so deleting a note in one test could affect counts in another. The new tests only delete notes they created themselves, and the existing count test compares against a 'before' value, so this works today.
impact.fix: Nothing needs fixing now. Keep each test deleting only notes it made.

concepts.name: function
concepts.explain: A named set of instructions you can run again and again, like a recipe card. deleteNote is a function.

concepts.name: return value
concepts.explain: The answer a function hands back when it finishes. deleteNote hands back true or false.

concepts.name: true / false (boolean)
concepts.explain: A value that can only be yes (true) or no (false), like a light switch that is on or off.

concepts.name: id
concepts.explain: A unique label for each note, like a ticket number, so the program knows which note you mean.

concepts.name: note store (notes)
concepts.explain: The place in memory where all notes are kept, like a box of index cards. It has built-in actions such as get, delete and values.

concepts.name: export / import
concepts.explain: export lets one file share a function. import lets another file use it. The test file imports deleteNote from notes.js.

concepts.name: test
concepts.explain: A small piece of code that checks another piece of code does the right thing, like a quiz for your program.

concepts.name: node --test
concepts.explain: A command that runs all the tests in the project with Node.js and reports how many passed or failed.

quiz.explain: There is nothing to delete, so it returns false. The test 'returns false when deleting a note that does not exist' checks this.

quiz.q: Why is deleteNote only one line long?
options: Because notes.delete already removes the item and returns true or false
Because the agent forgot to finish it
Because it uses git to delete the note
quiz.explain: The note store's own delete action already gives the exact answer the user wanted, so deleteNote just passes it back.

quiz.q: You delete the same note twice in a row. What do you get each time?
quiz.explain: The first call removes the note (true). The second call finds nothing to remove (false).
